issues.description: The Electron version in use is affected by published security advisories that are fixed in newer releases (46: GHSA-3c8v-cfp5-9885, GHSA-3p22-ghq8-v749, GHSA-4f78-qhmw-8j8m, GHSA-4p4r-m79c-wq3v, GHSA-532v-xpq5-8h95, ...)
issues.consequence: The Electron version in use lacks published security fixes; some of them are exploitable by web content (see the advisories).
issues.interaction: Depends on each advisory
issues.remediation: Upgrade Electron to the newest release of a supported major version, then re-run the scan.

issues.description: No CSP has been detected in the target application
issues.consequence: Without a Content Security Policy, injected markup can run inline script. A strict CSP is what turns an HTML injection into a harmless one.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Serve a Content-Security-Policy with every page, from a <meta> tag or the response headers, and start strict.
issues.remediationExample: session.defaultSession.webRequest.onHeadersReceived((d, cb) => cb({ responseHeaders: { ...d.responseHeaders, 'Content-Security-Policy': ["default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'"] } }));

issues.description: Evaluate the implementation of the navigation limits (will-navigate, will-frame-navigate, setWindowOpenHandler): the will-navigate handler never calls event.preventDefault(), so it blocks nothing
issues.consequence: Windows can be navigated to any site (e.g. by a link in shared content); that site then runs inside the app window, with its preload and IPC access.
issues.interaction: A click on a crafted link
issues.remediation: Block navigation away from your own pages and route external links through an allowlist.
issues.remediationExample: win.webContents.on('will-navigate', (e, url) => { if (new URL(url).origin !== ownOrigin) e.preventDefault(); });

issues.description: Missing will-navigate navigation limit
issues.consequence: Windows can be navigated to any site (e.g. by a link in shared content); that site then runs inside the app window, with its preload and IPC access.
issues.interaction: A click on a crafted link
issues.remediation: Block navigation away from your own pages and route external links through an allowlist.
issues.remediationExample: win.webContents.on('will-navigate', (e, url) => { if (new URL(url).origin !== ownOrigin) e.preventDefault(); });

issues.description: Permission handler: setPermissionRequestHandler grants every permission to every origin
issues.consequence: Without a permission handler, any page (including one reached through a link in shared content) gets camera, microphone, notifications and other permissions automatically.
issues.interaction: Viewing the content is enough when it runs as script; a click when it is a link
issues.remediation: Set both permission handlers, allow only what the app needs and only for your own origin, and deny everything else.
issues.remediationExample:
ses.setPermissionRequestHandler((wc, permission, cb, details) => cb(permission === 'notifications' && new URL(details.requestingUrl).origin === ownOrigin));
ses.setPermissionCheckHandler((wc, permission, origin) => permission === 'notifications' && origin === ownOrigin);

issues.description: Do not allow insecure HTTP connections (<script> http://cdn.example.com/app.js)
issues.consequence: Content loaded over plain http can be modified by anyone on the network path (Wi-Fi, proxy).
issues.interaction: None: an attacker on the network path acts while the app talks to its servers
issues.remediation: Load every script, style, frame and API over HTTPS (and WebSockets over wss://).

issues.description: Disable nodeIntegration for untrusted origins (nodeIntegration is enabled)
issues.consequence: Page script has full Node.js access: any XSS in this window is code execution on the user's machine.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Turn nodeIntegration off and move Node.js work into the main process behind narrow IPC handlers, with a preload script for the bridge.

issues.interaction: None: an attacker on the network path acts while the app talks to its servers
issues.remediation: Load every script, style, frame and API over HTTPS (and WebSockets over wss://).

issues.description: The nodeIntegration flag is enabled for the application, but some resources are loaded over an unencrypted connection.
issues.consequence: Plain http content is loaded into a window with Node.js: someone on the network path gets code execution on the machine.
issues.interaction: None: an attacker on the network path acts while the app talks to its servers
issues.remediation: Load only HTTPS content, and turn nodeIntegration off for any window that shows remote content.

issues.description: No Electron Fuses configuration found. RunAsNode, NODE_OPTIONS, --inspect and ASAR integrity fuses are insecure by default (electron-builder)
issues.consequence: Build hardening left at insecure defaults. It matters to someone who can start or modify the app on the device (e.g. RunAsNode turns it into a Node.js interpreter), not to other users' content.
issues.interaction: Access to the user's device or account
issues.remediation: Flip the insecure fuses at package time with @electron/fuses.
issues.remediationExample: flipFuses(exe, { version: FuseVersion.V1, [FuseV1Options.RunAsNode]: false, [FuseV1Options.EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable]: false, [FuseV1Options.EnableNodeCliInspectArguments]: false, [FuseV1Options.EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation]: true, [FuseV1Options.OnlyLoadAppFromAsar]: true, [FuseV1Options.EnableCookieEncryption]: true, [FuseV1Options.GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges]: false });

issues.description: The <webview> tag is enabled
issues.consequence: The <webview> tag is enabled: script injected into the page can create webviews with its own settings.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Avoid <webview>; if it is required, remove nodeintegration, disablewebsecurity and allowpopups, set a partition, and validate src.

issues.description: The <webview> tag is enabled but no will-attach-webview handler verifies webview options before creation
issues.consequence: A <webview> embeds other content; misconfigured, that content runs with Node.js or preload access.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Avoid <webview>. Use an iframe with sandbox, or a WebContentsView/BrowserView with contextIsolation and sandbox on. If it must stay, lock it down in will-attach-webview.

issues.description: Do not allow insecure connections, by explicitly opting-out from TLS validation or importing untrusted certificates (every certificate is accepted, TLS validation is disabled)
issues.consequence: Certificate verification is overridden: someone on the network can impersonate the server if the check is too lenient.
issues.interaction: None: an attacker on the network path acts while the app talks to its servers
issues.remediation: Do not return success (0) for every certificate in setCertificateVerifyProc; verify the chain, or fall back to Chromium's result (-3), and reject mismatches (-2).

issues.description: The Electron version in use is no longer supported and does not receive security fixes: Electron 11 (supported: 44, 43, 42)
issues.consequence: This Electron version no longer receives security fixes, including for flaws exploitable by web content.
issues.interaction: Depends on each advisory
issues.remediation: Upgrade Electron to a currently supported major version; unsupported versions get no security fixes.

issues.sample: webPreferences: { nodeIntegration: true, contextIsolation: false, webSecurity: false, sandbox: false, webviewTag: true, preload: path.join(__dirname, 'preload.js') }

lines: webPreferences: { nodeIntegration: true, contextIsolation: false, webSecurity: false, sandbox: false, webviewTag: true, preload: path.join(__dirname, 'preload.js') }

issues.description: Use sandbox for untrusted origins
issues.consequence: The renderer is not sandboxed: page content exploiting a Chromium bug escapes to the operating system more easily.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Turn the renderer sandbox on (the default since Electron 20) and do not combine it with nodeIntegration.

issues.description: TLS certificate validation is disabled for Node.js connections (NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 or rejectUnauthorized: false) (in the npm script "start": it applies when the app is started with that script, typically in development; a packaged build does not run npm scripts)
issues.consequence: TLS certificate checks are off for Node.js requests: someone on the network can impersonate the servers the app talks to.
issues.interaction: None: an attacker on the network path acts while the app talks to its servers
issues.remediation: Remove NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 and fix the certificate problem itself (trust the right CA, use a valid certificate).

issues.description: Do not allow popups in webview
issues.consequence: The content shown in this <webview> can open new windows, e.g. for phishing or to get around navigation limits.
issues.interaction: Viewing the content is enough when it runs as script; a click when it is a link
issues.remediation: Remove the allowpopups attribute from the <webview>, or handle new-window requests and deny what the app does not need.

issues.description: Review the use of custom command line arguments: --ignore-certificate-errors
issues.consequence: Chromium switches that weaken security (e.g. disabling web security or certificate checks) apply to all content the app shows.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Remove switches that weaken the browser (--no-sandbox, --disable-web-security, --ignore-certificate-errors, --remote-debugging-port, --disable-site-isolation-trials) from app.commandLine and the launcher.

issues.description: Review the use of the contextIsolation option (contextIsolation is disabled)
issues.consequence: Page script shares its JavaScript world with the preload: an XSS in this window can tamper with the preload and reach its privileged APIs, often up to Node.js.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Turn contextIsolation on (the default since Electron 12) and give the page only what it needs through contextBridge in the preload script.
issues.remediationExample: webPreferences: { contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false, sandbox: true, preload: path.join(__dirname, 'preload.js') }

issues.description: Do not use disablewebsecurity
issues.consequence: The same-origin policy is off: script in the page can read data from any site and local files.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Remove webSecurity: false; fix cross-origin needs with CORS headers or a request handler instead.

lines: webPreferences: { nodeIntegration: true, contextIsolation: false, webSecurity: false, sandbox: false, webviewTag: true, preload: path.join(__dirname, 'preload.js') }

issues.description: Window security settings: BrowserWindow (nodeIntegration on, contextIsolation off, sandbox off, webSecurity off, preload preload.js)
issues.consequence: Each window's effective security settings.
issues.interaction: Not applicable

issues.description: DevTools are opened programmatically; ensure this cannot happen in production builds (always opened, including in production builds)
issues.consequence: DevTools can be opened in the shipped app: someone at the keyboard can inspect and run code in the app's context. Other users' content cannot use this.
issues.interaction: Access to the user's device or account
issues.remediation: Disable DevTools in production builds.

issues.description: Review the use of custom protocol handlers (request-derived file paths have no relevant pre-operation containment guard; validate traversal and caller access)
issues.consequence: A custom protocol serves files: crafted URLs in content may read files outside the app (path traversal).
issues.interaction: Opening a crafted deep link
issues.remediation: Treat deep-link URLs as untrusted: parse them, allow only known actions and hosts, and never pass them to loadURL, a shell or a file path unchecked.

issues.description: setWindowOpenHandler allows new windows to be created; verify that only trusted URLs are allowed (every URL is allowed to open a new window)
issues.consequence: window.open() and target=_blank links in page content open app windows the app does not vet (phishing, getting around navigation limits).
issues.interaction: A click on a crafted link
issues.remediation: Deny new windows by default and open only allowed HTTPS URLs in the system browser.
issues.remediationExample: win.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler(({ url }) => { if (isAllowed(url)) shell.openExternal(url); return { action: 'deny' }; });

issues.description: Review the use of openExternal (the value comes from a window.open() call or link in web content and is not validated)
issues.consequence: A URL is handed to the operating system: if page content controls it, a crafted link (file:, smb:, a custom protocol) in shared content can launch programs or leak credentials.
issues.interaction: A click on a crafted link
issues.remediation: Parse the URL and open it only for allowed schemes and hosts; never pass raw page input to shell.openExternal.
issues.remediationExample: const u = new URL(url); if (u.protocol === 'https:' && allowedHosts.has(u.hostname)) shell.openExternal(u.href);

properties.source: a window.open() call or link in web content

issues.description: IPC handler does not appear to validate the sender (event.senderFrame) before acting on the message
issues.consequence: The IPC handler does not check which page sent the message: script injected into any window, or a foreign page the window navigated to, can call it with the app's privileges.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.howToValidate: Manual: read the handler and check that it verifies event.senderFrame (its URL or origin) before acting. A watch session lists the origins that used each channel, and whether content carrying the marker reached it.
issues.remediation: Check who sent the message before acting on it: compare event.senderFrame.url's origin with your own, and ignore other frames.
issues.remediationExample:
function validateSender(frame) { return new URL(frame.url).origin === 'app://main'; }
ipcMain.handle('ch', (e, ...args) => { if (!validateSender(e.senderFrame)) return; /* … */ });

issues.description: IPC handler: 'run' uses processes with arguments from the page (command); no rejecting input guard was recognized by this analysis; operations: process at main.js:26; argument checks: command not-recognized
issues.consequence: What a page can make the main process do through this channel: script injected into a window that can reach it inherits these capabilities.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Validate the shape and type of every argument in the main process, give each channel one narrow job, keep shell, file and window access out of handlers that take page input, and never send credentials back to the page.

issues.description: A child process is started with a dynamic command (exec receives data from an IPC message from a renderer)
issues.consequence: Data from a page or an IPC message reaches a shell command: content that gets a message to it can run programs on the user's machine.
issues.interaction: Whatever sends the data (often a click or a document)
issues.remediation: Never build a command line from input. Use execFile or spawn with an argument array and no shell, validate each argument against an allowlist, and prefer a library call to a command.

properties.source: an IPC message from a renderer

issues.description: IPC handler: 'open' uses shell with arguments from the page (file); no rejecting input guard was recognized by this analysis; operations: shell-openPath at main.js:27; argument checks: file not-recognized; path containment not recognized for file
issues.consequence: What a page can make the main process do through this channel: script injected into a window that can reach it inherits these capabilities.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Validate the shape and type of every argument in the main process, give each channel one narrow job, keep shell, file and window access out of handlers that take page input, and never send credentials back to the page.

issues.description: Review the use of shell.openPath with non-constant paths: opening attacker-influenced paths can execute files (the value comes from an IPC message from a renderer and is not validated)
issues.consequence: A path is opened with its default program: if page content or an IPC message controls it, it can run an executable or script on the machine.
issues.interaction: Opening a crafted attachment or file
issues.remediation: Resolve the path against a base folder, reject anything outside it, block executable extensions, and prefer shell.showItemInFolder over opening the file. Check the result string, because openPath returns an error message instead of throwing.
issues.remediationExample: const full = path.resolve(base, name); if (!full.startsWith(base + path.sep) || /\.(exe|bat|cmd|ps1|js|lnk|msi|scr)$/i.test(full)) return;

issues.description: Do not allow insecure connections, by explicitly opting-out from TLS validation (every invalid certificate is accepted)
issues.consequence: Invalid TLS certificates are accepted: someone on the network can impersonate the server and inject content.
issues.interaction: None: an attacker on the network path acts while the app talks to its servers
issues.remediation: Do not call callback(true) for the certificate-error event. Let the load fail, and pin the expected certificate if a private CA is used.
issues.remediationExample: app.on('certificate-error', (event, wc, url, error, cert, callback) => { callback(false); });

issues.description: Powerful Electron/Node.js APIs are exposed to the renderer through contextBridge (exposes ipcRenderer)
issues.consequence: The preload exposes powerful APIs (e.g. raw ipcRenderer) to the page: any script injected into the page (XSS) can use them.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.remediation: Expose one narrow function per action through contextBridge, validate its arguments in the main process, and never expose ipcRenderer, require or send/on wrappers that accept any channel name.

issues.description: API exposed to web content: window.ipc (value that can't be listed statically)
issues.consequence: What the preload exposes to pages: everything an XSS in those pages could call.
issues.interaction: Not applicable

issues.description: Global object exposed by an assignment: window.render assigned; whether untrusted pages receive it depends on the script context and isolation
issues.consequence: Direct global assignments found in source. Whether an untrusted page receives them depends on the script context and isolation.
issues.interaction: Not applicable

issues.description: HTML is built from dynamic data; unsanitized input leads to XSS in the renderer (innerHTML with a dynamic value)
issues.consequence: Dynamic data is inserted as HTML: if it can hold content stored by another user, their markup runs as script in this window (XSS).
issues.interaction: Viewing the content
issues.howToValidate: Automatic: in a watch session (electronegativity --app <install folder>), save content carrying the HTML marker the tool prints, in the fields this code shows, then view it. If the markup reaches this code, the finding is confirmed at this location.
issues.remediation: Write text with textContent or a framework binding instead of innerHTML, document.write or insertAdjacentHTML. Where HTML is required, sanitize it with DOMPurify first.

issues.description: The Chromium 87.0.4280.141 in this Electron version misses 4280 upstream security fixes (400 critical, 2013 high), 51 of them for vulnerabilities exploited in the wild (CISA KEV: CVE-2025-10585, CVE-2021-30633, CVE-2021-37973, CVE-2022-3075, CVE-2022-4135); 40 backported fixes are already subtracted. Upgrade Electron.
issues.consequence: The browser engine inside the app misses security fixes; the renderer bugs among them are exploitable by any web content the app shows, and those in CISA's KEV list are exploited in the wild.
issues.interaction: Depends on each advisory
issues.remediation: Upgrade Electron to a release whose Chromium includes the fixes (newest release of a supported major version), and re-run the scan.
